factSheet.title: AI in Nollywood: how Nigerian filmmakers are using AI tools, and the questions they face

claims.text: Nigerian filmmakers and digital creators are using AI to cut costs, expand storytelling possibilities and compete globally, industry insiders told Forbes Africa.
In March 2026, a YouTube-backed workshop in Lagos introduced filmmakers including Biodun Stephen and Omoni Oboli to Flow, an AI filmmaking tool developed by Google.
Filmmakers at the workshop said AI could help them visualise scenes before filming, speed up conceptualisation and simulate scenes that would be expensive or difficult to shoot.
Actor and producer Omoni Oboli says she has used AI tools to generate story ideas, animate videos and create promotional materials.
Travel and lifestyle creator Tayo Aina says he has used generative AI to recreate historical moments in his documentary-style videos when archival footage was unavailable.

For the film Eshugbayi Eleko, AI was used to create establishing shots and briefly reconstruct Lagos as it looked in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with some AI-generated sequences lasting only a few seconds, a filmmaker told NewsCrackers NG.
The Naija Artificial Intelligence Film Festival, founded by Obinna Okerekeocha, received 490 submissions for its debut, according to TechCabal.

article:
> **Key takeaways**
>
> - Nigerian filmmakers and creators are using AI to cut costs, expand storytelling and compete globally, industry insiders told Forbes Africa. [c1]
> - A YouTube-backed workshop in Lagos in March 2026 introduced filmmakers to Flow, Google's AI filmmaking tool. [c2]
> - The Naija Artificial Intelligence Film Festival received 490 submissions for its debut. [c7]
> - Makemation, a Nigerian film about AI, was released in cinemas in 2025 and has toured festivals and universities. [c9]

## The landscape shift

Nigerian filmmakers and digital creators are using AI to cut costs, expand storytelling possibilities and compete globally, industry insiders told Forbes Africa. [c1]

In March 2026, a YouTube-backed workshop in Lagos introduced filmmakers including Biodun Stephen and Omoni Oboli to Flow, an AI filmmaking tool developed by Google. [c2] Filmmakers there said AI could help them visualise scenes before filming, speed up conceptualisation and simulate scenes that would be expensive or difficult to shoot. [c3]

## How filmmakers are using it

### On set and in post

- Actor and producer Omoni Oboli says she has used AI tools to generate story ideas, animate videos and create promotional materials. [c4]
- For the film Eshugbayi Eleko, AI was used to create establishing shots and briefly reconstruct Lagos as it looked in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with some AI-generated sequences lasting only a few seconds, a filmmaker told NewsCrackers NG. [c6]
- Travel and lifestyle creator Tayo Aina says he has used generative AI to recreate historical moments in his documentary-style videos when archival footage was unavailable. [c5]

### On screen and at festivals

- Makemation, produced by Nigerian AI developer turned filmmaker Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, was released in Nigerian cinemas in 2025 and has toured international festivals and universities. [c9]
- Its producers describe AI as both a storytelling subject and part of the production workflow, combining generative AI systems with live-action filmmaking. [c10]
- The Naija Artificial Intelligence Film Festival, founded by Obinna Okerekeocha, received 490 submissions for its debut, according to TechCabal. [c7]

## Limits

NewsCrackers NG says transparency about AI use could become increasingly important in Nollywood as audiences encounter more AI-generated images, voices and scenes. [c11]

## What comes next

Okerekeocha says he wants to train thousands of African AI filmmakers over the next five years and support tools trained on local languages, voices and cultures. [c8]
